issues.legal_issue: A consent decree obtained through a fraudulent process against an illiterate and vulnerable claimant is a nullity.
material_facts: The claimant was an illiterate, childless widow who relied on her brother-in-law to help record inherited property in her name.
The earlier suit’s plaint, written statement, evidence and decree were all prepared or completed on the same day, without a credible explanation for how the claimant had appeared and consented.
The claimant’s lawyer was professionally associated with the opposing side’s lawyer, and the brother-in-law’s account of payment for the property was unsupported and inconsistent with the pleadings.
After the decree, a purported caveat was treated as an independent proceeding; the claimant was summoned and made to state that she would not challenge the decree.
The trial court found fraud, while the appellate court accepted the decree as valid and the High Court dismissed the further appeal without addressing the material circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The consent decree was obtained through a systematic fraud and was a nullity; the appellate and High Court judgments were set aside and the trial court’s judgment was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Fraud puts an end to everything, and a decree obtained by fraud is a nullity. The Court also observed that a caveat under Section 148-A of the Code of Civil Procedure is not an independent proceeding on the basis of which the court issues summons and records a statement as occurred here. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: civil_suit_challenges_prior_consent_decree and claimant_was_illiterate_and_vulnerable and same_day_suit_and_decree and (claimant_was_induced_to_sign_without_understanding or caveat_followed_by_summons_and_recorded_statement)

predicates.civil_suit_challenges_prior_consent_decr: The proceeding is a civil suit challenging an earlier consent decree.
predicates.claimant_was_illiterate_and_vulnerable: The claimant was illiterate and relied on another person who was able to influence or take advantage of the claimant.
predicates.same_day_suit_and_decree: The earlier suit’s pleadings, evidence and decree were completed on the same day.
predicates.claimant_was_induced_to_sign_without_und: The claimant was led to sign or mark court papers without understanding that they would result in a decree against the claimant.
predicates.caveat_followed_by_summons_and_recorded_: A caveat was followed by summons to the claimant and the recording of a statement about whether the decree would be challenged.

issues.definition: When a civil suit challenges a prior consent decree and the claimant’s vulnerability and the circumstances of the proceedings show that the claimant was induced to participate without understanding or was brought before the court through an irregular caveat process, the decree is a nullity.

issues.legal_issue: A suit challenging a decree is within limitation when the cause of action arises from the opponents’ later interference with the claimant’s possession and assertion of the decree, and the claimant sues shortly thereafter.
material_facts: The claimant alleged that the opposing side began interfering with her possession and asserting the decree about two and a half months before she filed the challenging suit.
The trial court found that the cause of action arose when the opposing side began interfering with her ownership and possession and asserting that it had a decree in its favour.
The Supreme Court rejected the conclusion that the suit was out of time merely because it was filed years after the decree.
issues.conclusion: The suit was within limitation because the cause of action arose when the opposing side interfered with the claimant’s possession and asserted the decree, shortly before the suit was filed.
issues.legal_principle: On the facts, the relevant cause of action arose from the later interference with possession and assertion of the decree, not merely from the date on which the decree had been made. The Court cited no limitation provision or earlier case for this conclusion.

rule.if: civil_suit_challenges_prior_decree and opponents_interfered_with_claimant_possession and opponents_asserted_prior_decree and claimant_sued_shortly_after_interference

predicates.civil_suit_challenges_prior_decree: The proceeding is a civil suit challenging an earlier decree.
predicates.opponents_interfered_with_claimant_posse: The opposing side later interfered with the claimant’s possession of the property.
predicates.opponents_asserted_prior_decree: The opposing side relied on the earlier decree as a basis for its claim to the property.
predicates.claimant_sued_shortly_after_interference: The claimant filed suit shortly after the interference and assertion of the decree.

issues.definition: When a suit challenges a prior decree and the opposing side later interferes with possession and asserts that decree, a claimant who sues shortly after those events has brought the challenge within limitation.
